question: What foundation depth is required for the sign posts drawn in Figure 2A-2?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The evidence does not specify any required foundation depth for the sign posts shown in Figure 2A-2. Figure 2A-2 and Section 2A.15 address mounting heights and lateral offsets (e.g., 5-foot and 7-foot minimum heights, 12-foot and 6-foot lateral offsets), while Section 2A.18 addresses posts and foundations only in performance terms — no numeric foundation depth is given anywhere in the provided material. Standards (mandatory): - "Sign posts, foundations, and mountings shall be so constructed as to hold signs in a proper and permanent position, and to resist swaying in the wind or displacement by vandalism." (This is a performance requirement; it does not prescribe a specific depth.) - For context on what Figure 2A-2 actually illustrates: "In rural areas, the minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement, of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 5 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." - "In business, commercial, or residential areas where parking, bicyclist, or pedestrian movements are likely to occur, or where the view of the sign might be obstructed, the minimum height... of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 7 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 2A-2 shows minimum mounting heights (5 ft, 7 ft, 4 ft to plaque, 17 ft overhead) and lateral offsets (12 ft, 6 ft, 2 ft minimums) but includes no dimension for post embedment or foundation depth. [Image 4] (the same Figure 2A-2 in full-page view) likewise shows no foundation depth dimensioning. [Image 2], [Image 3], and [Image 5] show related mounting-height figures (Figure 2M-3, Figure 2A-1, Figure 6F-1), none of which specify a foundation depth. Citations: - Section 2A.18 Standard §1 (p.60) - Section 2A.15 Standard §4 (p.58) - Section 2A.15 Standard §5 (p.58) - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) The evidence is insufficient to state a required foundation depth; the MUTCD material provided imposes only the general requirement that foundations hold signs in a proper and permanent position.
